LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_PostRider.title: royal post rider
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_PostRider.description: [PAWN_nameDef] carried the royal post from station to station, changing horses at every one and sleeping in the saddle. [PAWN_pronoun] has crossed the whole satrapy more times than [PAWN_pronoun] can count.
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_Weaver.title: carpet weaver
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_Weaver.description: [PAWN_nameDef] knotted carpets in a workshop of twenty looms, a pattern of a thousand flowers held in [PAWN_possessive] head. A single carpet of [PAWN_possessive] hangs in the satrap's hall.
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_Gardener.title: paradise gardener
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_Gardener.description: [PAWN_nameDef] kept a royal garden: four beds, four channels, a thousand roses and the satrap's favourite pomegranate tree, which [PAWN_pronoun] talks to.
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_Immortal.title: immortal guard
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_Immortal.description: [PAWN_nameDef] stood in the royal guard, one of the ten thousand whose number never falls. [PAWN_pronoun] learned to fight in a line, to obey without a word and to look splendid while doing it.
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_Dabir.title: court secretary
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_Dabir.description: [PAWN_nameDef] wrote the satrap's letters in three scripts and read everyone else's. [PAWN_pronoun] knows which governor owes what to whom, and never says it aloud.
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_Qanat.title: qanat digger
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_Qanat.description: [PAWN_nameDef] dug water tunnels under the mountains by lamplight, reading the slope by a plumb line and the air by the flame. [PAWN_pronoun] is not afraid of the dark or of hard rock.
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_Astronomer.title: court astronomer
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_Astronomer.description: [PAWN_nameDef] measured the stars from a palace roof, kept the calendar and was asked to read the future far more often than [PAWN_pronoun] wanted to.
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_Merchant.title: road merchant
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_Merchant.description: [PAWN_nameDef] led camel caravans along the royal road with silk going one way and silver the other, and haggled in every language spoken between the two ends.
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_BazaarChild.title: bazaar runner
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_BazaarChild.description: [PAWN_nameDef] ran errands in the covered bazaar, carrying tea, change and gossip between the stalls.
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_HorseChild.title: horse herder
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_HorseChild.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up on the summer pastures with the royal herds and could ride before [PAWN_pronoun] could walk properly.
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_LoomChild.title: loom child
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_LoomChild.description: [PAWN_nameDef] sat beside [PAWN_possessive] mother at the loom, cutting knots and learning the patterns by their names.
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_CourtPage.title: court page
LanguageData.HE_Pars_BS_CourtPage.description: [PAWN_nameDef] served at the satrap's table and learned how to bow, when to speak and how to listen to what was not said.
